title: Reconcile live Supabase security state before treating projections as safe
desired_change: Document and remediate live Supabase security findings that are currently invisible to PR #3: RLS-enabled tables without policies, the vector extension installed in public, and public.rls_auto_enable() exposed as a SECURITY DEFINER function callable by anon and authenticated roles. Define which tables are API-exposed, which are private projections, explicit grants and policies, extension placement, privileged-function boundaries, and advisor-based release checks.
expected_outcome: The Quirk Supabase projection layer has an explicit, reviewable security contract and cannot inherit unsafe or ambiguous access behavior from historical database state.

risk.rights_or_safety_impact: Ambiguous Data API exposure and privileged database functions can create unauthorized access or mutation paths, while RLS-without-policy can make intended access assumptions false in either direction.

hidden_context_dependencies: A competent outsider cannot infer which RLS-enabled public tables are intentionally inaccessible versus accidentally missing policies.
The live project exposes a SECURITY DEFINER function public.rls_auto_enable() to anon and authenticated roles, but no repository policy explains or justifies that authority.
The vector extension is installed in the public schema despite the current security advisor warning, with no documented exception.
The PR does not define Data API exposure, grants, policy ownership, or security-advisor acceptance criteria for its proposed projection tables.
acceptance_checks: Every API-exposed table has an explicit access decision, grants, and RLS policy set appropriate to its ownership model.
Every intentionally private table is demonstrably inaccessible to anon and authenticated roles.
public.rls_auto_enable() is removed, converted to an appropriate invoker model, or moved/revoked with explicit justification and tests.
The vector extension warning is remediated or accepted through an explicit documented waiver with evidence.
Supabase security advisors show no unresolved tribunal-created WARN finding before release.
A clean-environment operator can explain and reproduce the Supabase access model without Bryan.
